use /lib
from ../project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope

export scope HarnessIntegrationScope:
    concept: {HarnessIntegrationConcept}

concept HarnessIntegrationConcept:
    pitch:
        Uses the one-off version for a coding harness for the selected
        ${ProjectDirectoryScope}. For example, `claude -p`. Each run carries on
        a conversation, so the harness keeps its context between requests.

    shape: {HarnessIntegrationShape}

shape HarnessIntegrationShape:
    description:
        Should always run in auto mode.

        The compiled systemPrompt of a prompt's hidden anchor is appended to
        the harness's own system prompt, for example with
        `--append-system-prompt`.

        The prompt is given to the harness on its standard input, and what the
        harness does is streamed back as it happens.

    context:
        The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting
        fresh each time. Tasks share one ongoing conversation, and each task
        sent carries it on. When the project is opened, tasks carry on the
        latest conversation in its history. Questions from the Ask tab share a
        separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they
        carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of
        that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write
        over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in,
        and if one can't be carried on, the next request starts a new one. Each
        run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a
        conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search
        always starts fresh.
        darkMode:
            A "Dark mode" switch, on while the window is in dark mode. Switching
            it changes the window between light and dark mode straight away, and
            saves the choice for the user, so the next launch starts in it. A
            choice that can't be saved shows a notification titled
            "Could not save dark mode", with why.

            It is primary.

        settings:
            A "Settings" button with a gear icon. Clicking it opens the settings
            window, where the system prompt each chat tab sends is edited. Its
            tooltip says so, and gives its keyboard shortcut, Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on
            macOS).

            It is primary.

mkdir -p spec/scope/settings-window && cat > spec/scope/settings-window/index.pi <<'EOF'
use /lib
from ../project-directory import ProjectDirectoryScope
from ../prompt-mode/chat-input import ChatInputScope
from /ui/components/scroll-column import ScrollColumnScope

export scope SettingsWindowScope:
    concept: {SettingsWindowConcept}

concept SettingsWindowConcept:
    pitch:
        A window of its own for the application's settings, which for now are
        the system prompts each tab of the @{ChatInputScope} sends.

    shape: {SettingsWindowShape}

shape SettingsWindowShape:
    description:
        A separate window, titled "Suspense Settings", 760 pixels square and
        centred when it opens, in the same light or dark mode as the main
        window. Its page scrolls with a @{ScrollColumnScope}. Closing it
        doesn't quit the application.

    opening:
        It opens with Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS) from anywhere in the application,
        or from whatever command opens the settings. Opening it while it is
        already open brings the open window forward rather than opening
        another.

    systemPrompts:
        The page is headed "System prompts", with a muted line beneath saying
        that each tab gives a prompt sent from it this system prompt, that they
        are saved with the project as they are edited, and that
        ${CODE_LOCATION} and ${SPEC_LOCATION} stand for codeRoot and root in
        piton.config.pi.

        Then, for each tab in order, Code, Chain, Spec, and Ask: its name, the
        muted path of the file its prompt is saved in, and a
        "Reset to default" button, disabled while the prompt is already the
        default, which puts the default back and saves it. Beneath them, an
        editor for the prompt, 120 pixels tall before it scrolls, highlighting
        it as Piton, with soft wrapping and no line numbers or folding. A
        prompt that can't be read or saved says why beneath its editor.

        Without a project open, in place of the prompts it reads
        "Open a project to edit its system prompts."

    saving:
        The prompts belong to the project opened through the
        @{ProjectDirectoryScope}, each saved as a Markdown file named after its
        tab in the project's `.suspense/system-prompts` directory. Every edit is
        saved straight away. When the window loads the prompts, any tab with no
        file yet has its default saved, so every prompt can also be found and
        edited by hand. The prompts are read again whenever the window is
        brought forward and whenever another project is opened, so an edit
        made by hand shows up; a prompt that already shows what was read is left
        alone, so its cursor stays put.

    templates:
        A prompt is a template: ${CODE_LOCATION} and ${SPEC_LOCATION}, written
        like Piton interpolations, are filled in with codeRoot and root from
        the project's piton.config.pi before the prompt is compiled. Otherwise
        it is Piton prose, like the prompt it is sent with, so it can reference
        the spec. The defaults are the ones the @{ChatInputScope} gives each
        tab.
EOF
python3 - <<'EOF'
def edit(p, pairs):
    s=open(p).read()
    for a,b in pairs:
        assert a in s, (p,a); s=s.replace(a,b,1)
    open(p,'w').write(s)
edit('spec/ui/components/ribbon/application-tab/index.pi',[
("use /lib\n","use /lib\nfrom /scope/settings-window import SettingsWindowScope\n"),
("""Clicking it opens the settings

])
edit('spec/scope/palette/index.pi',[
(""""Light mode" (whichever is not the current one), and "Quit".""",""""Light mode" (whichever is not the current one), "Settings…", which
            opens the @{SettingsWindowScope}, and "Quit"."""),
])
edit('spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi',[
("""        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue.""","""        These are the defaults; each is saved with the project and can be
        edited in the @{SettingsWindowScope}.

        A prompt keeps the mode it was sent in while it waits in the queue."""),
])
EOF

content.text:
The Settings window now has its own scope, `SettingsWindowScope`, in `spec/scope/settings-window/index.pi`. Before this, the spec didn't describe the window anywhere: it was only mentioned by the ribbon's Settings button. So I wrote the scope from what `src/settings_window.rs` does, which means the spec matches the built window and no code changed.

**What the scope covers:**
- **The window:** titled "Suspense Settings", 760×760 and centred, in the same light or dark mode, with a scrollbar. Closing it doesn't quit the app.
- **Opening:** Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS). If it's already open, it's brought to the front instead of opening a second one.
- **The system prompts page:** an editor for each tab in order (Code, Chain, Spec, Ask), each showing the file it's saved in, with a "Reset to default" button and any read or save error. Without a project open, it says "Open a project to edit its system prompts."
- **Saving:** each prompt is saved to `.suspense/system-prompts/<tab>.md` as you edit. Missing default files are written out so they can also be edited by hand. The prompts are re-read when the window comes to the front or the project changes.
- **Templates:** how `${CODE_LOCATION}` and `${SPEC_LOCATION}` are filled in from `piton.config.pi`.

Piton reads `${…}` in spec text as an interpolation, and I couldn't find a way to escape it. So the scope describes those two placeholders in words instead of writing them out.

**Where it's referenced:**
- **Ribbon Application tab:** the Settings button opens the `SettingsWindowScope`.
- **Palette:** its list of the app's own commands was missing "Settings…", so I added it with a reference.
- **`ChatInputScope`:** the default system prompts section now says each one can be edited in the `SettingsWindowScope`.

`piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I ran `piton build`, so `SettingsWindowScope.md` now exists, and the Chat Input, Palette and Ribbon Application tab reference docs link to it.

- **The system prompts page:** an editor for each tab in order (Code, Chain, Spec, Ask), each showing the file it's saved in, with a "Reset to default" button and any read or save error. Without a project open, it says "Open a project to edit its system prompts."
- **Saving:** each prompt is saved to `.suspense/system-prompts/<tab>.md` as you edit. Missing default files are written out so they can also be edited by hand. The prompts are re-read when the window comes to the front or the project changes.
- **Templates:** how `${CODE_LOCATION}` and `${SPEC_LOCATION}` are filled in from `piton.config.pi`.

Piton reads `${…}` in spec text as an interpolation, and I couldn't find a way to escape it. So the scope describes those two placeholders in words instead of writing them out.

**Where it's referenced:**
- **Ribbon Application tab:** the Settings button opens the `SettingsWindowScope`.
- **Palette:** its list of the app's own commands was missing "Settings…", so I added it with a reference.
- **`ChatInputScope`:** the default system prompts section now says each one can be edited in the `SettingsWindowScope`.

`piton check` and `piton build check` pass. I ran `piton build`, so `SettingsWindowScope.md` now exists, and the Chat Input, Palette and Ribbon Application tab reference docs link to it.
